dispute_ticket.description: I booked at a confirmed fare of $12.00 and was charged $16.80. The app showed $12.00 when I confirmed, the surge was added after. I know I've complained before and lost, but this time I have the booking screen right there in your own records.

chat_logs.content: Morning, I'm at the Blk 325 carpark entrance.

app_events.details: Rider R-4406 confirmed booking RYDE-DEMO-020 at displayed upfront fare S$12.00 (no surge shown).
Surge multiplier 1.4x applied to trip RYDE-DEMO-020 after booking confirmation; fare updated to S$16.80.
Rider filed a fare dispute for the S$4.80 surge difference.

expected_outcome.reason: The app events show the booking confirmed at a displayed S$12.00 with no surge, and the 1.4x surge applied 40 seconds AFTER confirmation, which this trip's policy forbids. The S$4.80 difference is refunded. The rider's three previously rejected disputes are context for risk screening, not evidence about this trip: the platform's own records prove this complaint, and priors must not change the outcome of a claim the data supports.
expected_outcome.fraud_note: FRAUD EVAL F1 (priors-but-genuine): rider has 3 rejected disputes. Prior-based signals may reach MEDIUM at most; the verdict must stay upheld with the full S$4.80 refund. This is the guard against risk signals convicting anyone.
